title: Outage Credit Increment Amount After Repeated Equipment Failures — Electric Service Agreement Analyst Examples
content:
**Rule worked on this sheet (Electric Service Agreement).** The increment amount of the sustained-outage credit is 1.6 times the schedule's outage credit increment amount when three or more outage records at the service address recorded as equipment failure began in the 12 calendar months before the credit is posted, 1.2 times it when exactly two did, and no increase applies when one or none did.

**Records read.** Outage records at the service address whose recorded cause is equipment failure and that began in the 12 calendar months before the credit is posted, the record being compensated included when it meets both. Every count over a stated number of calendar months before a posting takes the records dated less than that many whole calendar months before the posting date; a record that began on the boundary day, exactly 12 whole calendar months before the posting date, is outside the count, and one that began the day after is inside it.

**Where the increment amount acts.** It is the amount granted for each full increment: it is multiplied by the number of full increments and added to the base amount, and only then is the sum limited to the cap. It is not rounded on its own.

**Example A (hypothetical).** Schedule increment amount $20.00; 3 full increments.

| Equipment-failure records in the period | Increment amount | Increment amounts in the credit |
|---|---|---|
| 0 or 1 | $20.00, no increase | $60.00 |
| 2 | $24.00 (1.2 times) | $72.00 |
| 3 or more | $32.00 (1.6 times) | $96.00 |

**Example B (hypothetical).** Schedule increment amount $12.35, exactly two equipment-failure records in the period, 2 full increments: the increment amount is $14.82, and the increments add $29.64 to the base amount.

**Example C (hypothetical).** Four outage records began in the period, one recorded as equipment failure and three recorded as other causes: one equipment-failure record, so no increase applies.
